display.title: The Last Shabbos of the Year: A Blessing for the Whole Year
display.summary_short: During Selichos, Uncle Yossi explains why the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah brings Hashem's blessing for the entire coming year, and why we say Tehillim that morning.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show during the days of Selichos. Uncle Yossi explains that Hashem blesses us constantly: some blessings last an hour or a day, some a week or a month. But the last Shabbos of the year brings a blessing that lasts the whole coming year. As the Zohar teaches, Shabbos is the source of blessing for the days that follow, and as we sing in Lecha Dodi, it is 'the source of blessing'. Since Rosh Hashanah falls in the next week, its blessing is included in this Shabbos, so everyone rises early to say Tehillim in shul. As the Baal Shem Tov taught, on this Shabbos Hashem Himself blesses the month, giving us the strength to bless every new month all year. Selichos prepare us: we ask forgiveness, Hashem answers 'I have forgiven', and with a clean record we ask to be written in the Book of Life, hoping for Moshiach and next year in Yerushalayim.
display.lesson: The Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah is a source of blessing for the whole year; prepare for it with Selichos and Tehillim.
